storyboardBeats.narration: Your tire wear has a shape — and that shape can point to what's wrong.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Extreme macro low-angle shot of a tire tread, camera slowly rotating around the circumference revealing an uneven wear pattern silhouette against dramatic raking side light, shallow depth of field, cinematic automotive commercial look, 9:16 vertical framing

storyboardBeats.narration: Wear straight down the center often means overinflated. Wear on both edges often means underinflated.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Split macro comparison of two tire treads mounted on a rotation stand, no hands, even studio lighting, slow lateral pan from a center-worn tread to an edge-worn tread, 9:16 vertical framing

storyboardBeats.narration: One edge wearing more, or a feathered saw-tooth texture — that usually means alignment, not air.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Extreme macro of a feathered, saw-tooth tread wear pattern, raking side light exaggerating the texture, slow push-in, shallow depth of field, moody garage-bay backdrop, 9:16 vertical framing

storyboardBeats.narration: Cupping — little scalloped dips around the tire — that's one clue a shock or strut is wearing out.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Macro shot of a tire tread showing cupping (scalloped dip wear), camera slowly orbiting the tire surface, dramatic rim light catching the shadow inside each scallop, 9:16 vertical framing

storyboardBeats.narration: Send this to someone whose tires look uneven. Stop by and we'll take a look — Nick's Tire and Auto.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Wide shot of a tire shop garage bay interior, alignment rack visible in the background, bay door partially open to daylight, no readable signage or branding in frame, warm late-day light, static hold, 9:16 vertical framing
